subject: DPA clarifications & follow-up — data residency, subprocessors, breach notice
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@zenith.ai>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@zenith.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications & follow-up — data residency, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Use case summary: real-time summarization and search over customer support transcripts (PII in some inputs).
- Key asks you raised: data residency (can we keep data in us-east-1), control-plane vs data-plane roles, subprocessors list & notification commitments, breach notice timing, and retention/logging controls for request logs and user content.

Attached is our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) and a short SOC 2 summary. High level answers below — happy to pull in legal/security for language redlines: 

1) Controller / Processor: Redwood acts as processor for request payloads customers send to the API; customers (Zenith AI) are controllers of their end-user data. We call this out explicitly in section 2.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a list of subprocessors and provide 30 days notice for new ones; we can provide Zenith's security contact with the current roster and a commitment to notify you. If you require a prior-approval workflow for new subprocessors we can discuss (some customers accept notification + opt-out window).

3) Breach notice: Standard contract language we propose is "as soon as reasonably possible" with a 72-hour initial notification for security incidents impacting customer data. We can accept a 72-hour SLA for notification in the DPA.

4) Data residency: Hosted customers can pin their data-plane region to specific cloud regions (e.g., us-east-1). For Dedicated/Private deployments we offer in-region tenancy. We should discuss expected retention windows and whether you need a contractual guarantee for residency.

5) Logging & retention: Default request logs (metadata + audit logs) retained 30 days; payload-content retention is configurable depending on your plan and regulatory needs.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share the DPA (attached) with the redline option; Nikhil (CC) will confirm technical controls and default retention values.
- If that looks good, we can share a DocuSign link and schedule a short call with your legal/security to finalize language.

Attachments:
- Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (PDF, 182 KB)
- SOC2-Summary.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@zenith.ai>

Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@zenith.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & follow-up — data residency, subprocessors, breach notice

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side so we can prep legal: 

- Subprocessors: can you provide the current roster as a spreadsheet and confirm the notice cadence (you mentioned 30 days)? Also, will Redwood allow us to object to a new subprocessor and require a mitigation plan / alternate routing if objection accepted?

- Breach notice: great on 72 hours initial notification. Can you confirm what information is included in that initial notice (scope, affected accounts, mitigation steps) and whether you provide a post-mortem with timelines?

- Data residency: we need a contractual guarantee that customer data (both content and backups) for our org remain in us-east-1. Is that supported on the hosted plan or would we need Dedicated/Private? If hosted, are there any failover policies that could move data between regions in an outage?

- Retention/Logging: you mentioned default 30 days for request logs. For compliance we need the option to reduce to 0 days for payload retention and to configure longer audit log retention (up to 1 year). Is that configurable per account via the console or is it a support/legal workflow?

If you can answer these we’ll route to our procurement team. Happy to jump on a short call with your security/legal folks if helpful.

—Samir
Head of Platform Security, Zenith AI
samir.khan@zenith.ai
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@zenith.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@zenith.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2027 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & follow-up — data residency, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Samir / team —

Quick tech-run answers to Samir's bullets: 

- Subprocessors: I’ll attach the current roster separately (operations-maintained list). Our standard process is 30 days notice for additions. We support an objection window; for enterprise contracts we can add contract language requiring prior approval for a defined set of categories (e.g., analytics providers).

- Breach notice: Initial notification includes summary of impacted services, affected customer identifiers, known timeline, and immediate mitigation steps. We follow-up with a detailed incident report and timeline within 14 business days where feasible. We can include this in DPA language.

- Data residency: For hosted customers we offer region pinning of data-plane (control plane remains global). This is available for customers on committed plans (e.g., Dedicated) or with an enterprise addendum. In the rare failing-over scenarios we replicate minimal control-plane metadata for orchestration; we can commit in contract that content and backups remain in us-east-1 unless you opt into a multi-region DR policy.

- Retention/Logging: Payload retention is configurable; we can set default to 0 days on a per-customer basis (no retention of content) or longer. Audit/log retention up to 1 year is supported via a console setting for Dedicated customers; for hosted customers we can offer configuration via Support/Account.

Technical attachments (sent via secure link): subprocessors_roster.csv, incident_response_overview.pdf

If legal wants to redline the DPA we’re happy to accept tracked changes. Priyom (CC) is our solutions engineer and can set up a demo of the console retention settings.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Platform Security & Ops, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com

Appreciate the quick responses — that helps a lot. Two asks to move forward: 

1) Please send the subprocessors_roster.csv and incident_response_overview.pdf to our security mailbox (security@zenith.ai) and I’ll share with procurement/legal.
2) Can you produce a short DPA redline that:
   - locks data residency to us-east-1 for content and backups,
   - states 72-hour initial incident notification with a 14-business-day follow-up report,
   - adds a prior-approval workflow for new subprocessors in the agreement for our org (we can provide a list of critical categories).

If you can send a DocuSign link after you attach the redline we can fast-track this on our side. Proposed next meeting: Thu 18 Mar 09:00 PT to run legal/security questions.

Thanks —
Samir
